articles.title_orig: Novaya Gazeta, Fiercely Independent Russian News Outlet, Says It Will Shut Down
articles.title_zh: Novaya Gazeta, Fiercely Independent Russian News Outlet, Says It Will Shut Down
articles.content_orig:
Independent outlet, whose former editor Dmitry Muratov won Nobel prize, cites intolerable pressure from authorities
Europe live – latest updates
Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s best-known independent media outlets, has announced it will permanently close next month. The newspaper, whose former editor-in-chief Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel peace prize in 2021 , cited intolerable pressure, including being stripped of its newsroom, its donation platforms and its legal right to publish.
“This is not just our own story; it is the story of a country and a society that are being systematically crushed,” wrote its editor-in-chief, Sergei Sokolov, on the newspaper’s website.
Launched in the 1990s and for many years partly funded by the late Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, Novaya made its name through dogged, long-form reporting on corruption, rights abuses and social issues. Over the years, six of its journalists have been assassinated, including Anna Politkovskaya, who was gunned down in the stairwell of her Moscow apartment block in 2006.
While Novaya always swam against a tide of repression, the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 made independent reporting almost impossible and decimated the Russian media landscape. Novaya was one of the last critical voices still operating from inside the country.
“For nearly five years of ***, we managed to keep working while being completely encircled by the security services. Now it’s over. We have found ourselves in a ‘kill zone’,” wrote Sokolov. The stars were used in place of the word “war”, as under Russian law, journalists must refer to the war in Ukraine as a “special military operation” or face consequences.
The newspaper’s first response to the invasion was to put out a special bilingual Russian-Ukrainian edition in the days after Vladimir Putin launched the invasion. It described the war as “madness” on its front page. Soon after, the Kremlin implemented draconian new censorship laws, which forced media outlets to publish only the Russian official narrative about the conflict.
“We said it’s not journalism and we’re not going to do that,” said Nadezhda Prusenkova, the head of Novaya’s press service. The newspaper published blank white spaces instead of euphemisms and false information, to provide a visible reminder of the censorship laws.
By the end of March 2022, Novaya decided to stop publishing its print edition altogether, but the threats and pressure only increased. In April that year, Muratov was doused with red paint while on a train , an attack that damaged his eyesight and that US officials say was carried out on the orders of Russian intelligence agencies. In September that year, the newspaper’s official licence was taken away and soon after their website was blocked in Russia.
Novaya’s journalists, long used to operating in a hostile environment, found ways to circumvent the bans. Many left Russia, and a number of exiled former employees set up Novaya Gazeta Europe , a legally distinct outlet. Muratov and a core team stayed behind and continued to publish a series of magazines with a print run of 999 copies, taking advantage of a law that means magazines with under 1,000 copies do not require an official licence. Novaya’s website continued running, too, although the Russian state hit the outlet with various new legal threats.
“The fact Novaya kept working for this four and a half years after everything that happened was a miracle, but it was not just a miracle, it was also the daily choice of people who continued to go to work even when it was very scary,” said Elena Kostyuchenko, a former Novaya journalist who spent 17 years at the newspaper. “Today I feel very inspired by my colleagues, but also very painful and sad for them, and for all of us.”
after newsletter promotion
In recent months, Prusenkova said the pressure had become intolerable. In April, the journalist Oleg Roldugin was arrested and charged with “unlawful access to computerised information”. He is under house arrest awaiting trial and last month Sokolov’s home was searched as part of the case.
This month, the newspaper’s landlords informed Novaya staff that they must vacate their longstanding office premises in central Moscow by 9 November. The newsroom has been the hub of the newspaper for decades and houses a memorial museum to Politkovskaya in the former office of the murdered journalist. Prusenkova said the exhibits would be taken down and put into storage, for now.
On top of the eviction notice, all the outlet’s donation platforms have been shut down, leaving the paper without any source of funding. The court case, combined with the eviction and the lack of funds, gave the newspaper no choice but to close, said staff.
“Sometimes it happens that your enemies win. At this moment in time, it seems like they have won, and we have no options left,” said Prusenkova. But she said it was probable Novaya’s journalists would try to find some way to continue their work. “After all, we don’t know how to do anything else,” she said.

articles.title_orig: Goodwill Seemingly Has No Clue It’s Selling a Previously Unknown Leica Prototype Lens
articles.title_zh: Goodwill Seemingly Has No Clue It’s Selling a Previously Unknown Leica Prototype Lens
articles.content_orig:
An exceedingly rare Leica prototype lens is up for auction right now. No, it’s not at Leitz Photographica or Wetzlar Camera Auctions. It’s at Goodwill .
Per Lenstag’s founder, Trevor Sehrer, this lens appears to be a previously unknown second copy of a very rare prototype lens that most recently sold for nearly $50,000.
In 2021, PetaPixel reported on what was then believed to be a one-of-a-kind prototype: the Leica / Hughes Leitz 17mm f/2. Leica Store Lisse was selling the 26-pound behemoth lens for $47,200. This same lens had been listed on eBay four years prior for $24,000, as Leica Rumors wrote in January 2018.
A Leica / Hughes Leitz 17mm f/2 prototype lens, which looks identical to the one sold in 2021 except for its C530-0004 model number rather than the C530-0007 one seen five years ago, is somehow at Goodwill of the Great Plains in Sioux Falls, South Dakota right now.
It’s being sold in “as is” condition. It seems Goodwill doesn’t fully appreciate what it has on its hands, listing it like a regular lens instead of the treasure it is.
”We do our best to describe items completely and accurately, but we are not experts,” Goodwill warns, adding that prospective bidders should look very carefully at the included photos, as they are effectively serving as the product’s description.
Even if the Leica / Hughes Leitz 17mm f/2 lens available right now at Goodwill is not in great condition — although it does look good — it remains an exceptionally collectible piece of photographic history.
People have stumbled upon incredible Leica gear in unusual places before. Last year, Ontario photographer Brandon Simpson found a $2,000 Leica at a thrift store for $10 . A teenager in 2021 found an entire Leica M kit for $15 at a church sale. A few years before that, a college student grabbed a Leica M5 at a thrift store for just $5.
At the time of writing, Goodwill’s Leica / Hughes Leitz 17mm f/2 prototype lens is $3,008 after seven bids . While it’s much pricier than the thrift store finds above, it may still sell for what amounts to a steal. The bidding ends at 9:50 PM ET (6:50 PM PT) today, October 30. Good luck.

Hackers working for the North Korean regime have been blamed for a record cryptocurrency heist following a cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance . The hackers stole at least $6.3 billion in crypto from the company’s wallets, though about half of that amount was frozen as the stolen crypto traveled across various blockchains, according to security researchers.
The breach is by far the largest known theft of crypto in history, though the incident has not been confirmed yet to be resolved, and the amount of crypto stolen may change.
In a post on X , Binance said its initial investigation showed that the hackers broke into the company’s network after targeting a “compromised” Binance engineer’s laptop, which “allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”
Binance said it has seen no evidence of a leak of its private keys, which would grant the hacker near-unfettered control over the company’s stores of crypto.
The crypto exchange — the world’s largest — said it has now suspended all deposits and withdrawals while its investigation into the breach continues. TechCrunch reported on Thursday that the exchange had paused withdrawals across some of its blockchains.
Binance said “user funds are safe,” but did not immediately provide proof of this claim. The company said it will “publish an updated proof of reserves once the remediation is complete.”
Spokesperson Andie Cooper said in a statement shared with TechCrunch on Friday that some $3 billion has been frozen by industry partners. The spokesperson said Binance has “begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.”
It’s unclear how the hack went down or under what circumstances the employee’s laptop was compromised, but it’s not uncommon for security incidents to stem from the use of compromised software on employee devices.
Software is generally built from many components, including open source projects, which hackers regularly target , compromise and modify in order to steal data from devices that the affected software is installed on. Other times, malware bundled with regular-looking apps and games can allow hackers to steal usernames, passwords, and session tokens from infected computers, which may let them log in as if they were a legitimate employee.
Binance will face questions about why the company’s security allowed a single employee’s laptop to access systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in funds.
Spokespeople for Binance did not respond to an email with questions about the breach. TechCrunch has also asked the company who, if anyone, performed a security audit of Binance’s network and systems prior to the hack. Companies regularly ask third-party companies to stress-test their security to identify weaknesses that could be exploited by attackers, but it’s unclear if Binance sought such a review.
Security researchers at TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and forensic company, attributed the breach to North Korean hackers, and called it the “largest hack in history.”
Researchers describe the network of hackers, known in the cybersecurity industry as TraderTraitor, as a North Korean cell focused almost exclusively on stealing crypto from large companies and exchanges. This group was also blamed for the now-second-largest heist on record, a $1.4 billion theft from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025 .
According to TRM, the theft of Binance’s billions in crypto took about 20 minutes.
Blockchain security firm Elliptic also attributed the Binance theft to North Korean hackers. Elliptic said some of the stolen funds ended up in the same wallet that was used in a previous cyberattack on crypto exchange Bitget earlier this year, in which hackers stole $351 million .
The U.S. government and its allies have long warned about the threat from North Korea, which remains cut off from the U.S. and the global financial system for its ongoing development of its nuclear weapons program. Researchers say the breakaway country’s sole motivations are to steal as much crypto as possible in order to continue developing its sanctioned weapons of mass destruction.

articles.title_orig: Kimmel, Fallon, Jon Stewart & More Make Big Changes for Midterm Elections Night
articles.title_zh: Kimmel, Fallon, Jon Stewart & More Make Big Changes for Midterm Elections Night
articles.content_orig:
The hosts of late-night television won’t be reacting live to the results of the upcoming midterm elections, with none of the nightly shows scheduled for live episodes on Tuesday (November 3).
According to LateNighter , the likes of Jon Stewart , Seth Meyers, and Jimmy Fallon won’t air live episodes as the midterm results come in, ending a 24-year streak dating back to 2002 and Stewart’s live episode of The Daily Show covering that year’s results.
NBC won’t be airing The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon or Late Night With Seth Meyers on November 3, instead preempting them with live news coverage of the midterm results. CBS will be doing the same, meaning no episodes of Byron Allen’s Comics Unleashed .
ABC will air a new episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live! in its usual 11:35 p.m. time slot, but it will not air live. The show is expected to tape later than usual, per LateNighter, so that Kimmel can react to some of the early East Coast results. However, ABC may cut away from the broadcast for breaking news coverage.
Network sources told the outlet that if results that determine control of the House or Senate come in during Kimmel’s show, the program may be interrupted for live ABC News reaction.
Comedy Central will also be airing a new episode of The Daily Show on Tuesday night, but it is expected to be taped before the polls close in New York.
While live late-night reaction to midterm results has been a staple for over two decades, the amount of coverage has dwindled in recent years. In November 2018, Trevor Noah ‘s Daily Show , CBS’ The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, Jimmy Kimmel Live! , and Late Night all covered the first midterm election of Donald Trump ‘s presidency.
That number dropped in 2022, when only Colbert and Kimmel broadcast live shows on election night. For 2026, that number has now dropped to zero, with no late-night show scheduled to broadcast live reaction.

articles.title_orig: Nintendo Cancels Kirby Air Riders Halloween Event Following Performance Woes
articles.title_zh: Nintendo Cancels Kirby Air Riders Halloween Event Following Performance Woes
articles.content_orig:
If you have been keeping up with Kirby Air Riders of late, you might have been excited to dive into the game's new Halloween event this weekend and pick up some spooky Ghost headwear while you're at it. Well, we're sorry, but that's not going to happen, as Nintendo has cancelled the event.
The event was originally scheduled to run from 28th October through until 4th November, but many players reported nasty technical difficulties when taking part in early matches, where the screen would regularly freeze — which, in a game as frantic as Air Riders, isn't going to cut it.
You can see the issue for yourself below (shared on Bluesky by TAHK0 ):
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 854k
This time, Nintendo didn't have a quick fix up its sleeve, so it decided to cancel the event instead. "We have confirmed an issue in the currently ongoing event 'Trick or Treat!' where the screen temporarily freezes during gameplay," a message from the Japanese Nintendo Support social media account (via machine translation) read this morning. "For this reason, we will be cancelling this event."
While Nintendo went on to apologise for the cancellation, it claimed that there are plans to hold the event again in the future, so everyone can get in on the themed reward. There's no official news on when it will return at the moment, but we have to imagine it will be sooner rather than later.

articles.content_orig:

Ukraine has ended a two-week pause on strikes against Russian oil refineries, according to monitoring channels, targeting the Novokuybyshevsk oil refinery in Russia 's Samara region overnight with a drone attack.
According to the Kyiv Independent, monitoring channel Exilenova+ published photos and videos showing a fire at the refinery, as well as witness reports of drones overhead.
Earlier it was reported that Ukraine's military had paused its strikes on refineries in response to weeks of pressure from US president Donald Trump , who blames such attacks for high diesel prices in the States.
On Thursday a Russian drone attack killed 14 people at the main ⁠railway station in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro , hitting a platform crowded with ⁠people boarding ​a ⁠train, officials said.
And both Russia and Ukraine said that demining operations around the Russian-held town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine had been completed and that an operation to bring aid and allow residents to leave was ready to begin.
Efforts have been underway for several weeks to organise ⁠a relief operation for the acutely deprived town's residents, which Russian forces seized soon after Moscow 's February 2022 invasion of its smaller neighbour.
Residents of the Russian-held town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine began evacuating on Friday as part of a joint relief operation by the two sides, the first of its kind in four years and eight months of war.
Many questions have been asked about the humanitarian operation and its wider significance under a deal that US first lady Melania Trump was involved in brokering, with the additional involvement of Pope Leo.
Besides the safe evacuation of many of Oleshky's residents, Moscow and Kyiv are trying to use the operation to show US President Donald Trump they are serious about his efforts to secure an overall peace settlement.
Neither side wants to be blamed by Trump for something going wrong in Oleshky, an event that could burnish his self-professed credentials as a peacemaker before US midterm legislative elections.
But the two sides remain far apart on potential terms for ending the conflict in Ukraine, and there appears to be no immediate prospect of it ending.
Moscow hopes Trump can pressure Kyiv into agreeing a deal that meets many of its conditions, such as full Russian control of Ukraine's Donbas region.
Kyiv wants to ensure US intelligence sharing continues, along with full access to Elon Musk's battlefield communications system Starshield.
Vladimir Putin has said that Russia ⁠is prepared ‌for a potential war with Europe in his latest sabre-rattling threat against the continent, though ‌he claimed Moscow does not ‌want one.
The Russian president said his country would support any steps aimed at restoring relations with European countries, as he commented on his phone call with the leaders of Norway and Finland, which took place on Tuesday.
But in a chilling threat, he said that if tensions were to escalate too far, there “would be no winners”.
The Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta said on Friday that it was winding up its remaining operations after a campaign of state pressure in which a senior editor has been prosecuted and its financial support and premises have been taken away.
“We have been killed,” the publication, set up with money from the Nobel Peace Prize of the last Soviet leader, Mikhail Gorbachev, said in a statement.
The paper halted its print edition inside Russia in 2022, but had continued to produce online content and operate from its office in central Moscow.
There was no immediate comment from the authorities, which had designated the publication a "foreign agent".
But the Kremlin has said in the past that some censorship is necessary at a time when Russia is locked in what it describes as an existential struggle with the West over Ukraine.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Friday that European participation will be needed in the planned peace talks with Ukraine and the US.
Peskov said there were no detailed discussions about such participation at present.
Residents in the occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky began a desperate evacuation on Friday as a localised ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv held for a third day.
A fleet of 25 buses with at least 750 seats stood ready to withdraw locals seeking to leave, Kyiv's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said. His Russian counterpart, Yana Lantratova, added that space would also be provided for their pets.
Residents who wanted to leave were given a four-hour window to do so, lasting until 2pm local time (12pm GMT). Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay.
“Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to leave safely,” Lubinets said. “At the same time, those who have decided to stay can stay and will receive all the necessary humanitarian support.”
Evacuees were given a choice of evacuating to Ukrainian or Russian-controlled territory, but those headed for Ukraine would have to travel into Russian-held land and take a Russian government plane to Belarus before driving across the border into Chernihiv.
With the government urging Britons to prepare for emergencies and supplies of bottled water and tinned beans running low, food editor Hannah Twiggs put her appetite on the line to find out whether a week of tinned food and no cooking could be remotely bearable
The current Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries do not jeopardise the planned trilateral negotiations on peace in Ukraine, Russia's agency Interfax cites Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying.
Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries after a pause with the overnight attack on facilities in Samara region, Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said earlier on Friday.
Participation of European representatives in the planned peace negotiations between Russia, Ukraine and the United `States willbe needed at some stage, Russian agency Interfax quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying on Friday.
Mr Peskov said there were no detailed ‌discussions about ​such participation ‌at ⁠present.
Our world affairs editor, Sam Kiley, writes of the evacuation efforts in Oleshky:
“Four years of occupation by Russian troops, cut off from resupply and forced to eat grass in a frontline town, the survivors of Oleshky are now extras in a grandiose public relations operation for Melania Trump and her husband.
“ America’s first lady’s brokered deal – with the help of the Pope and hailed by the White House – sees suffering caused by Russia turned into a display by the Kremlin 's “humanitarian” leader while his troops resupply and rearm under the umbrella of a “ceasefire”.
“By Monday, the deputy governor of Kherson , the Ukrainian held city on the west bank of the Dnipro, says the killing will start again - and likely be worse.
“’We are very concerned that from Monday the Russians will start shelling Kherson heavily again,’ Oleksandr Tolokonnikov tells The Independent. ”

articles.title_orig: 'Bad time to troll': Binance cofounder Changpeng Zhao asks Elon Musk for 'respect' after post about bitcoin hack
articles.title_zh: 'Bad time to troll': Binance cofounder Changpeng Zhao asks Elon Musk for 'respect' after post about bitcoin hack
articles.content_orig:
The cofounder and former CEO of Binance asked Elon Musk not to "troll" the company on Friday and instead "show some support" after the SpaceX CEO appeared to mock the embattled cryptocurrency exchange in a series of social media posts.
After learning the world's largest crypto exchange had been hit by a $6.3 billion hack late Thursday, Musk posted several emojis, ranging from laughing to grimacing, on X.
In response, Changpeng Zhao reminded the SpaceX and Tesla CEO of Binance's equity stake in Musk's businesses.
Binance’s SpaceX stake, which stems from an earlier investment in what was then-Twitter, is worth more than $1 billion, Zhao said.
That's a tiny fraction of SpaceX's roughly $2 trillion valuation.
"Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop," Zhao wrote. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!"
It's not the first time the pair has sparred online.
In Nov. 2021, Binance suspended Dogecoin withdrawals because of a wallet glitch, a measure Musk called "shady". In reply, Zhao highlighted a major Tesla recall of almost 12,000 U.S. vehicles due to software glitches and hardware issues.
Binance froze all withdrawals and deposits after the hack, which investigators suspect to be the work of North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit TraderTraitor. It has since restored deposits.
Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far.

articles.title_orig: UK denies entry to Swedish academic due to speak at Palestine event
articles.title_zh: UK denies entry to Swedish academic due to speak at Palestine event
articles.content_orig:
London, United Kingdom – A pro-Palestine academic who was planning to travel to the United Kingdom has been denied entry because the government says his “presence in the UK is not considered to be conducive to the public good”.
The UK Home Office cancelled Swedish national Andreas Malm’s Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) on Wednesday, an email seen by Al Jazeera shows.
The decision came a week before Malm was due to appear on a panel organised by the British socialist magazine Tribune in London. Huda Ammori, cofounder of Palestine Action – which the UK has proscribed as a “terrorist” group – is also due to appear on the panel, which will be chaired by Hala Hanina of Palestine Deep Dive.
Malm, a climate activist and author who lectures at Lund University in Sweden, told Al Jazeera that he believes his ETA was cancelled because he was due to appear on the panel. He has contacted the Home Office for an explanation but is yet to receive a response.
“I have been going regularly to the UK for decades. My position on Palestine has always been public,” Malm said, adding that his latest visit to the country was in May.
“I haven’t said anything in public about Palestine during these intervening months or written anything about it. The only thing that could have caused this [latest UK decision] is that I was due to be on a panel on Wednesday evening, where I would talk to Huda Ammori of Palestine Action,” he said.
Malm used an ETA during his May visit to the UK, which allowed him to travel to the country again later in the year without seeking reauthorisation. He said he had received no indication from the Home Office that his ETA was at risk of being cancelled before receiving an email on Wednesday confirming that it had been revoked.
In its email, the Home Office told Malm that if he wishes to visit the UK, he needs to apply for a visa, after which the office will “consider your circumstances in more detail” before making a decision. However, the government website states that the processing time for a standard visitor visa is three weeks, meaning Malm would not receive it in time for next week’s panel even if his application were approved.
Travellers from countries whose nationals do not require a visa to visit the UK generally need an ETA. These include countries in Europe, the United States and Canada, among others.
The Home Office said it does not comment on individual cases.
“Decisions to refuse or cancel an ETA on the grounds that presence in the UK may not be conducive to public good are based solely on an assessment of the potential risk an individual may pose to UK society,” it said in a statement to Al Jazeera.
The cancellation of Malm’s ETA comes amid a wider crackdown on pro-Palestine activists by the UK government, something that began under then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer.
Tribune editor Oliver Eagleton said, “Andy Burnham’s government continues the authoritarian overreach we saw under Starmer. In this new dystopian Britain, it is now commonplace for authors and academics to be treated as terrorists because they support Palestinians facing genocide and the rights of people protesting that genocide.”
Starmer, a former human rights lawyer, was prime minister when the government proscribed Palestine Action last year.
The move classified the campaign group as a “terrorist” organisation under UK law, placing it on the same legal list as groups such as al-Qaeda and ISIL (ISIS). The proscription has been condemned by rights groups, including Amnesty International.
Most recently, Irish novelist Sally Rooney’s books were withdrawn from sale in the UK this month due to her public support for Palestine Action.
Rooney described Malm as a “brilliant and influential” intellectual.
“For the UK government to deny him entry to Britain is not only an outrageous attack on a respected climate expert, but a sad and frightening act of cultural self-harm,” she said.
Malm’s books include How to Blow Up a Pipeline: Learning to Fight in a World on Fire and The Destruction of Palestine Is the Destruction of the Earth.
Since Palestine Action was banned, more than 3,850 people have been arrested for publicly backing the group, in largely peaceful protests.
“This is a drift towards authoritarianism that didn’t begin with me and it’s not going to end with me either,” Malm told Al Jazeera. “If I’m now being deemed a threat to the public good because I’m supposed to have a conversation with someone from Palestine Action, this is guilt by association. Where does it stop?”
Gareth Dale, reader in political economy at Brunel University of London, told Al Jazeera that the Home Office’s decision suggests the UK government intends to continue suppressing free speech under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
“Andreas Malm is one of the world’s foremost campaigners on the two defining issues of our times – climate breakdown and the genocide in Palestine. Barring him from entry to the UK represents a monstrous attempt by the Burnham government to suppress free speech,” Dale said.
“Typical of bureaucratic tyranny, no reason was given for the ban; it is cynical and Kafkaesque. As Malm has committed no crime, we are left guessing as to the motives. Burnham cultivated the impression that his government would be turning a new leaf, but instead it is replicating Starmer-era authoritarianism.”

articles.title_orig: Did Apple and Amazon just save the smart display?
articles.title_zh: Did Apple and Amazon just save the smart display?
articles.content_orig:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.
Apple made a big splash early this October with its massive smart home announcement, including new Siri AI features, the company’s first smart display called HomeView and the long-awaited smart speaker , the HomePod Mini 2 .
Now Amazon’s here with its new Echo lineup, and we’re all comparing these smart speakers and smart displays with what Apple is offering. What’s interesting is that Amazon is taking a completely different path with its new home devices — especially the latest Echo Show, which is currently available for preorder . Here’s what that means and why it matters for potential buyers this holiday season.
Apple’s first smart display relies heavily on Siri AI and audio features as a selling point, with a design a bit like the Echo Show 11 . During Apple’s announcement, I noted this created dissonance since the 7-inch screen is too small to easily watch the latest Apple TV shows, or much else, even if the audio is excellent. That’s one reason companies like Amazon have been making Echo Show devices bigger and bigger.
Read more : How Does Apple’s HomeView Smart Display Look Against the Competition?
Now with the Echo Show 16, Amazon is embracing the idea of a second TV device for the kitchen or hallway more fully than ever. This new Show ditches the big speaker for a series of small woofers and tweeters (and a stand design perhaps pointedly reminiscent of Mac computers).
I’ll have to listen to the result in person, but it looks like Amazon is backing away from the 360-degree, room-filling sound for something that acts more like a traditional TV, while still including the touchscreen, camera and mic of past smart displays. It supports wall mounting if you’d rather not use a stand.
The Echo Show 16 backs up its new size and design with a built-in Fire TV platform, something previously limited to only larger, wall-mount-only Echo Shows. Fire TV not only makes it easier to access Amazon Prime content, but also handles third-party apps and more complex controls better.
Those deeply invested in catching up on shows or sports can upgrade to an enhanced Nanomatte display designed to cut glare and improve color accuracy. While Apple is a bit coy about which third-party apps will be supported alongside Apple TV, Amazon says the Echo Show will support Netflix, Disney Plus, YouTube, HBO Max/Peacock, Tubi and Pluto, which should reassure streaming fans.
The drawback to all this new tech is the price, something Apple HomeView fans will know well. While the small-screened HomeView starts at $299, Amazon’s Echo Show 16 starts at $499.99, and the Nanomatte display bumps the price up to $569.99. Plus, you’ll want a compatible stand, which starts at $69.99 but can go up to $150, so you can see how prices quickly rise.
That high price is a tough sell for anyone who already has a smart display or is leaning toward the HomeView, but people looking for a second Fire TV screen may find it more palatable. I want to test them both out before I make an ultimate recommendation.
The Echo Show 16 wasn’t the only Amazon device aimed at Apple’s latest releases. The company also announced a new Echo Studio model, starting at $249.99 and comparable to Apple’s HomePod Mini 2 — with one big difference. This latest Studio comes with a built-in, nearly invisible home camera.
Amazon says the camera is meant to gather visual intelligence for Alexa, which rings privacy warning bells to me, but the camera could let the voice assistant answer questions about what’s happening in the room when users are away or offer live views, sort of like a mini security camera .
I’m not convinced this camera add-on is worth it, but it does help Amazon differentiate the Studio from the $149 HomePod Mini 2, which might otherwise seem similar to the casual buyer.
Amazon also announced a noncamera Echo Dot, more affordable at $99.99, upgraded with an AZ3 custom-designed silicon chip for faster Alexa responses, and a kid’s version of the same model.
And while Apple may have showed how the iPhone Duo could be used as an impromptu alarm clock, Amazon showed up with its own dedicated smart clock, the aptly named Echo Time, a round, dial-like smart display meant to serve as a nightstand clock with the addition of Alexa Plus. It includes unique smart alarm features to help manage waking up in a slower fashion. But again, Amazon is setting prices very high at $199.99 for the clock .
I’d be remiss not to talk about Alexa Plus and how the AI voice assistant is now going head-to-head with Apple’s Siri AI. Both add new capabilities to the new smart displays. Siri AI gets home control functions and an easier way to display information pulled from emails, text messages and other iPhone sources.
Alexa Plus, meanwhile , will have a new interface on the Echo Show 16, which ditches the old transcription visual (which I kind of liked) and replaces it with an interactive display that can pull up visuals, videos, events and more as you talk with Alexa. Each conversation gets its own Card icon, so you can revisit and pick up past conversations as needed. Alexa also has a new Home Map mode which acts like a living layout of all your smart devices, letting you control what‘’’s on or off, room by room.
I already like Alexa Plus a bit more than Siri AI, even if the voice assistant gets a little too talkative, and now I’ll have new experiences to test out. Of course, cost is yet again a factor here: Apple notes that more advanced Siri AI features do require iCloud Plus subscriptions, although it’s still light on details. Alexa Plus, meanwhile, is free with an Amazon Prime subscription, but otherwise, it costs a steep $20 per month for most features.
Ultimately, Apple is treading carefully with its first-ever smart display, but that tiny screen is a tough sell for me. Amazon, meanwhile, is betting big that people want a second TV experience in their display and are willing to pay for it. Both AI voice assistants are showing up with new tricks I can’t wait to try.
Meanwhile, Amazon is trying out new avenues in the smart home, like giving its flagship smart speaker a built-in camera — which I’m dubious about — and releasing targeted screens for alarms, picture frames and more. It’s all very expensive, which gives Apple a surprise advantage for the holidays, but Amazon’s vision is strikingly different, so I’m not sure they’re after the same audience.

articles.title_orig: The Apple Pencil turned the Duo into my new favorite notebook
articles.title_zh: The Apple Pencil turned the Duo into my new favorite notebook
articles.content_orig:
Ignore the pile of previous favorite notebooks; this is the one that’s gonna change it all for me.
Ignore the pile of previous favorite notebooks; this is the one that’s gonna change it all for me.
Apple’s $2,000 folding phone is a surprisingly good stand-in for a $20 notebook.
Believe me; nothing gets me going quite like a new notebook. This one will be different, I think. This time, I really will take it everywhere. Inspiration can strike at any moment, and you have to be ready, says David Sedaris in that one MasterClass I watched on a flight. With this one special new notebook, I will see the world differently. I’ll steal moments for myself to write, rather than pulling out my phone to scroll at every opportunity like a trained monkey. And a few weeks, a month, or maybe a year later, I’ll concede that it didn’t change everything and add it to my notebook graveyard. At least they all look nice on the corner of my desk?
The iPhone Duo is not a notebook — although it is the first iPhone to support the Apple Pencil. Even so, I can see the new notebook effect in the eyes of the people I talk to about the Duo. “Is that the new iPhone?” the conversation starts. I hand over the phone and give them the short version of our 26-minute review : It’s nice, it’s kind of heavy and chunky, you should wait for the second generation. They nod, but I can tell they still want one anyway. They’re tired of their big/aging/boring phone, they tell me. And this one would be different.
It’s hard to argue against. It really is a different phone. Its new form factor lets you actually use it in meaningfully different ways. The Duo can act like a vintage Hasselblad with a waist-level viewfinder. It can be a book-shaped e-reader. And with this week’s iOS 27.2 update officially adding that Apple Pencil support, it can also be a notebook.
Notebooks are nice and help you express creativity. Phones are bad attention-stealing machines, or something.
That’s the USB-C Apple Pencil, to be specific, so there’s no pressure sensitivity. You do still get the ability to “scribble” handwriting that’s automatically turned into text in apps like Messages or Safari, as you can on the iPad. But even with the basic stylus, there’s a lot of fun to be had doodling and writing notes out by hand. I asked for some Pencil-friendly app suggestions and downloaded a handful. I used the native Notes app to scribble down some article ideas. I set my five-year-old loose on a blank note, to his delight (the phone survived the encounter, too). But having the stylus in my hand led me on an unexpected side quest: turning the whole phone into a notebook.
Why not? It’s notebook-shaped. Notebooks are nice and help you express creativity. Phones are bad attention-stealing machines, or something. Maybe I could cajole the Duo into being something less distracting, more input-friendly. I put together a minimalist home and lockscreen designed around this theory. I won’t lie, it’s pretty nice. But I don’t think I curated my way out of the new-notebook trap, even if it was a fun exercise.
There aren’t many apps ready to take advantage of the new stylus support. Notes, unsurprisingly, is where the Pencil is at its best. When you use the Pencil for handwriting in the app, you can enable the auto-refine handwriting feature that neatens up your writing while still keeping its unique characteristics intact. This has been available on the iPad since 2024 , and it’s particularly useful on the Duo’s comparatively small screens.
It occasionally gets tripped up by some of my scrawl that it either doesn’t know what to do with or misinterprets — it kept insisting on turning a “u” into an “o” in one instance. And it works after a small delay when you pause your writing, which I can see being distracting if I really want to get into a flow state. But it’s a nice middle ground between my untidy scribbles and full handwriting-to-text conversion and very handy for something like a grocery list.
The Notes app also has a big homescreen widget that kind of turned the phone into a notebook, but wasn’t nice to look at. After some more digging , I found almost exactly what I’d been looking for: TypeDraw .
It’s a $4.99 one-time purchase, and it’s optimized for the Duo. When you launch the app, it turns the cover screen into the front of your notebook. To flip to a page, you can either swipe on the cover screen or open the whole phone. It’s a delight.
TypeDraw isn’t really for power notetakers the way other apps like Bear are . You can’t add tags or links between notes, and you’re limited to one notebook. But it automatically creates a table of contents at the beginning based on the headings of your notes, so you can skip right to the section you’re looking for. Plus, if you drag your finger along the “elastic” on the cover, it’ll stretch and snap back, complete with satisfying haptics. I have zero regrets about the five bucks I spent on this app.
Using the Apple Pencil with the Duo gave me one more reason to love the matte finish on the inner screen. There’s just a bit of resistance moving the pencil across the display that feels more satisfying than the lifeless plastic-on-glass effect of writing on the cover screen. It’s not going to feel like using a Remarkable tablet or anything, but it’s nice.
The Pencil has one other neat trick — it can stick to the Duo’s hinge magnetically when the phone is closed. The pencil is longer than the phone, so it’s an awkward fit, but it’s been a handy way to carry both around the house as I relocate throughout the day.
I was only, like, 60 percent serious when I set out to turn the Duo into a notebook, but I actually liked the idea the more I got into it. Reimagining my homescreen around creating rather than consuming feels like a worthwhile cause, and I’m planning to live with it for a while to see if it inspires any changes in my phone habits. To that end, I also set up a shortcut to launch TypeDraw whenever I open the inner screen.
But I think the most useful part of this exercise was examining, once again, how much stuff I really need on my homescreen. I can get most things done with a Spotlight Search or a tap in the Control Center. Siri is much more helpful now too, and it’s always lurking nearby to help out. The grid of apps I’m so used to is mostly for emotional support at this point. I didn’t need a folding phone to learn that, but it helped.
Above all, the new-notebook effect proved to be just as strong as always. The shiny new thing eventually fades into the background. You certainly don’t need a $2,000 phone to reevaluate your homescreen. You can — and I will continue to — just carry a little notebook around with your regular phone. A fun new gadget is delightful, don’t get me wrong. But don’t hang all your hopes and dreams for a new you on one of them.
Photography by Allison Johnson / The Verge

articles.title_orig: Difficult negotiations lie ahead in Israel after Netanyahu’s bloc lost its parliamentary majority
articles.title_zh: Difficult negotiations lie ahead in Israel after Netanyahu’s bloc lost its parliamentary majority
articles.content_orig:
JERUSALEM — Israel’s final election results confirmed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc lost its parliamentary majority and that weeks of difficult negotiations among very different parties, from ultra-Orthodox Jewish to secular to Arab-led , lie ahead.
The results released early Friday showed Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday’s election. The main opposition bloc won 48. Arab-led parties secured the other 19, a historic showing. Now parties must meet, bargain and seek a way to team up for at least 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, remains in charge.
“Now comes the truly hard part,” centrist politician Yair Lapid said on X, urging patience and adding: “If you want to know if something’s happening behind the silence you’re hearing now, the answer is yes.”
The president will task someone with forming a government
Difficult decisions lie ahead. Will the main opposition parties that campaigned hard to unseat the divisive Netanyahu make the politically sensitive choice to partner with Arab-led ones? Or will they toss their vows aside to team up with Netanyahu in a potentially fractious unity government?
Friday is when much of Israel starts winding down for Shabbat, and it was not clear who might be meeting with whom. Israelis debated possible coalitions and challenges, as some expressed traditional wariness around Arab parties and others insisted it was time for Israel to take a deep breath and embrace them.
“There are options for all of this, not like in the United States, where there are only two parties,” said Beny Engalrd, a resident of Tel Aviv.
The election results still need to be certified and submitted to the president next Wednesday. Then President Isaac Herzog will task someone with forming the new government. That could be the leader of the party that received the most votes — Netanyahu — or whoever leaders of the various parties believe is best suited.
If multiple attempts to form a government fail, Israel faces a new election early next year. Herzog this week said he will do everything in his power to avoid that scenario.
Netanyahu and Likud target Arab parties without evidence
In the hours before final results were announced, Netanyahu and his Likud party amplified unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance.
The opposition quickly accused Netanyahu of demonizing the Arab population, which makes up 20% of the population and showed up at the polls like never before in outrage over Netanyahu’s far-right allies like National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. His party lost seats.
In Netanyahu’s first public comment Friday, he posted on X asserting it is forbidden to form a coalition with Arab parties.
The head of Israel’s election committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, had said “serious suspicions” of foreign interference had been brought before him. In a letter to the Shin Bet security agency, Sohlberg said he could not verify the claims but asked the agency to investigate.
Israeli media reported that members of Netanyahu’s party were accusing Qatar of involvement — a country that many Israelis view as a patron of Hamas, the Gaza-based militant group. Qatar issued a denial, calling the allegations “ridiculous and dangerous.”
As it announced results, the election commission said the investigation was based on classified intelligence. Acting Director General Dean Livne did not elaborate but warned that reports about the investigation had been “entirely unfounded.”
“It does not affect the final results that will be submitted to the president, nor does it concern any particular sector of the population,” he said.
By casting doubt on the vote, Netanyahu appeared to be trying to block any potential alliance between his opponents and the Arab-led parties. Netanyahu has suggested that it would be treasonous for chief rival Gadi Eisenkot or others to join with them.
The Shin Bet, seeking to calm tensions, said its investigation was not meant to “cast aspersions” on an entire section of the population that “exercised its right to vote in a democratic and lawful manner.”
The elections committee also sounded a note of caution in a letter written to a concerned member of parliament, saying that “allegations of systematic violations of electoral integrity are baseless.”
The committee wants findings from the Shin Bet within a week.
Opposition could assert control in the upcoming Knesset
Even as coalition negotiations begin, the new Knesset is expected to be sworn in Nov. 10. Once it convenes, Eisenkot’s bloc could join forces with the Arab parties to elect a new Knesset speaker, giving them control over the parliamentary agenda and potentially allowing them to advance and pass legislation before a new government is formed.
Already, hundreds of Israelis have been holding rallies urging Eisenkot and others to join forces with the Arab-led parties, a step that has happened only once before, briefly, in 2021.
“I believe we should join forces and cooperate with the Arab parties, a legitimate population in the state of Israel,” said Miri Sklair, a resident of Jaffa.
If Netanyahu loses office, that would set off a cascade of events that critics say he has desperately sought to avoid. He would be taken to account over yearslong corruption allegations, and an inquiry almost certainly would begin into security failures before the devastating Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack.

articles.title_orig: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid: Drives like an EV, but there’s no plug involved
articles.title_zh: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid: Drives like an EV, but there’s no plug involved
articles.content_orig:
For decades, car buyers in America have generally had access to four kinds of electrification. Most of the time, you can buy a battery electric car, a parallel hybrid car, a plug-in hybrid car, or, rarely, an extended-range electric car . In a weird, yet clever move, Nissan has gone a different direction. The 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid is an honest series hybrid, sort of like how a locomotive works. I got to drive it, and I feel like Nissan sort of created the best of both worlds in making a car that feels like an EV, but never needs to be plugged in.
For years, some car enthusiasts have considered Nissan to be a bottom-tier automaker of sorts. The poor reputation of early JATCO CVT-equipped Nissans arguably tarnished the brand’s reputation. It didn’t help when “ Big Altima Energy ” became an evergreen meme. Our comments still get populated with digs against Nissan CVTs.
Nissan has seemingly taken the criticism to heart, because from what I can see, the brand is going through a shocking turnaround on its product line. A couple of years ago, I found myself legitimately impressed with a rental-spec Rogue , and I’ve even found some joy in scooting around in base model Sentras, too.
But the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is on another level. I recently got to drive Nissan’s new moonshot in the mountains just outside of Santa Barbara, California, and my mind was blown by how much I enjoyed it. I’ll say it right now. If it were my own money, I’d buy a Rogue Hybrid over a Toyota RAV4 Hybrid. Yes, I said it.
( Full Disclosure : Nissan invited me out to Santa Barbara to try the new Rogue Hybrid. Nissan paid for my travel, an incredible stay at a Ritz-Carlton, and dishes of food so rich that I could barely pronounce their names.)
Engine : 1.5-liter ZR15DDTe fixed-compression turbocharged inline-three.
Transmission : Direct Drive.
Drive : Dual-motor all-wheel-drive.
Output : A generator making 146 horsepower and 171 lb-ft of torque, governed to 5,200 RPM. Plus a 202 horsepower front electric motor and a 134 horsepower rear motor. 225 horsepower combined system power.
Battery : 1.67 kWh lithium.
Fuel Economy : 41 MPG city, 36 MPG highway, 38 MPG combined.
Curb Weight : 4,107 pounds.
Base Price : $35,490 plus $1,595 destination fee.
Price As-Tested : $43,065 (SR Tech Package), before destination fee.
The Nissan Rogue Hybrid is a part of Nissan’s global strategy called Nissan Intelligent Mobility. Announced in 2016, Nissan Intelligent Mobility has become Nissan’s guiding vision for how to make its cars more convenient, greener, and more connected than before.
The biggest and most visible part of Nissan Intelligent Mobility is e-Power. Since 2016, Nissan has been developing a series hybrid technology that sets it apart from the competition.
In a typical hybrid car, a gasoline engine and an electric motor work in tandem to drive the vehicle. This is known as a parallel hybrid, and it’s the backbone for most hybrid cars. Some parallel hybrids don’t need to be plugged in, because the engine provides both locomotion and charging for the battery. Some parallel hybrids, known as plug-in hybrids, or PHEVs, have a sizable battery that gives the vehicle substantial all-electric range. When this range runs out, the engine kicks on, and driving then works similarly to how a regular parallel hybrid functions.
In a true series hybrid, the engine does none of the driving and cannot drive the wheels at all. Instead, all the engine does is act as a generator to provide electricity to an electric drive system. Today, series hybrids tend to be called extended-range EVs, and perhaps the most famous example is the BMW i3. The Chevrolet Volt is another great example, though its engine-generator can connect to the wheels in some situations.
Nissan admits that it doesn’t have the same brand image as its competitors in the hybrid space. Indeed, for many people, a Toyota is the default choice for a hybrid vehicle, and Toyota’s been churning them out for far longer than Nissan. Honda is probably the second choice for someone looking for a hybrid from a Japanese brand.
So, Nissan wanted to stand out in the crowd. It didn’t want to do the same thing as everyone else. Nissan also wanted to push the boundaries of what people expected from a hybrid. So, a decade ago, it went down the path of developing a series hybrid system.
Nissan says that the development of the original e-Power system was led by Naoki Nakada , who previously led the engineering behind the engine in the Nissan GT-R supercar. He was also the mind behind the original Nissan Leaf, and is on a mission to bring the GT-R experience to Nissan’s electrified lineup. Nissan continues with how he came up with the idea for e-Power:
The transition from traditional to fully electric mobility, however, won’t happen overnight. Some have hesitations toward EV ownership, such as driving range on a single charge, local and regional charging infrastructure, and cost. Realizing this, Nakada set out to ease customer concerns by developing an electrified powertrain that combines the thrilling performance of an electric motor with the ease of ownership a traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle offers. This is the origin of Nissan’s e-POWER technology.
Nissan e-POWER is different from typical hybrid systems as it simplifies the e-powertrain operation by having the high output electric motor solely provide power to the wheels. The lithium-ion battery powering the electric motor is recharged by a highly-efficient, on-board combustion engine acting as a power generator. For drivers, e-POWER offers a seamless and powerful acceleration experience similar to an EV, without the concern of a charging station. Instead, a visit to a gas station is all that’s needed to refuel. This makes electric mobility available to many more drivers than ever before.
Fuel efficiency is also at the core of Nissan’s e-POWER system with the engine operating at an optimized speed to recharge the battery. The engine is primarily activated at high cruising speeds or over rough road, when the sound of the engine can be masked by road noise. This ensures the driving experience is quiet like an EV in most driving scenes like a run around town.
Nissan’s e-Power system launched in Japan in 2016 in the Note city car, followed closely by the system getting fitted to the Serena minivan. Nissan’s tech has been a hit in Japan, and some 500,000 cars with an e-Power system were sold by 2021. Nissan e-Power cars are now sold in 68 countries, and Nissan says that it’s now made nearly two million of them.
But until now, no e-Power car has been sold in America. Nissan explains that the first two generations of e-Power were primarily developed for smaller vehicles and urban driving. It didn’t want to bring e-Power to America just yet because it knew that Americans liked bigger, faster cars, and wanted to feel comfortable driving them on the highway at high speeds.
Nissan has rectified that with the third-generation e-Power hybrid system. It’s designed to work specifically for larger cars and is engineered to gallop down an American superhighway. So, what car did Nissan put the new e-Power system into? Nissan selected its most popular vehicle in North America in one of its best-selling segments, the Rogue.
The Rogue enters an all-new generation in 2027, and at first, the new car will be hybrid-only. The pure internal combustion Rogue will continue on the old body for one more year before transitioning to the new body.
This new Rogue is going for a more dignified and upscale look than previous generations. Nissan says that this design is supposed to make the Rogue seem tough, refined, and fun all at the same time.
I really enjoy how much Nissan played around with hexagons. The grille and running lamps are hexagons, and I adore how both elements are blended together seamlessly. From a distance, it almost seems like the lights are emanating from the grille.

articles.title_orig: Police Scotland carrying out 'active inquiries' into Andrew and Epstein Balmoral visits
articles.title_zh: Police Scotland carrying out 'active inquiries' into Andrew and Epstein Balmoral visits
articles.content_orig:
Police in Scotland have opened an investigation into the time the former Prince Andrew spent with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his associate, Ghislaine Maxwell, at the king’s Balmoral estate.
Police Scotland, which provides law enforcement throughout the country, said on Friday that the inquiries began after it received “information” and that the investigation was at a “very early stage″.
The force provided no further detail about what the information was or what offences officers were investigating.
The investigation was first reported by The Daily Express, which said the inquiries were related to claims that women were trafficked to the king’s private estate in the Scottish Highlands.
“All inquiries are evidence-led, with the needs of victim survivors at the heart of those inquiries,″ Police Scotland said in a statement. “We would never confirm details of ongoing inquiries and it would be inappropriate to comment further.”
Images released by the United States Department of Justice appeared to show Epstein and Maxwell on a shooting trip at Balmoral in 1999. The photos were among millions of pages of documents the department published earlier this year as Congress probed Epstein’s links to politicians, business leaders and other influential people in the US and around the world.
The presence of anyone’s name or image in the files is not proof of wrongdoing.
Several other UK police forces, including London’s Metropolitan Police Service, Thames Valley Police and Surrey Police, are also investigating information released in the Epstein Files .
In February, Thames Valley officers arrested the former prince , now known as Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, on suspicion of misconduct in public office, based on information uncovered in the trove of documents released by US authorities.
The 66-year-old younger brother of King Charles III was held for several hours before being released on police bail pending further investigation.
It was the first time in nearly four centuries that a senior British royal had been arrested.
The former prince has repeatedly denied committing any crimes.
Mountbatten-Windsor’s links to Epstein have caused headaches for Britain’s royal family for almost two decades.
With US authorities preparing to release documents related to their long-running investigation into Epstein, the king late last year moved to shield the monarchy from the scandal by stripping his brother of his princely title.
Mountbatten-Windsor was also ordered to move out of the Royal Lodge , his longtime home in parkland near Windsor Castle. He now lives in a house at Sandringham, the king’s privately owned estate in eastern England.
The former prince’s reputation has been tarnished by his relationship with Epstein ever since 2008, when the wealthy American financier pleaded guilty to soliciting a minor for prostitution. In 2011, the late Virginia Giuffre alleged that she had been trafficked by Epstein and forced to have sex with Mountbatten-Windsor when she was 17.
Mountbatten-Windsor tried to silence the scandal by giving a lengthy interview to the BBC in 2019, but the strategy backfired when he was criticised for offering unbelievable explanations of his behaviour and failing to show empathy for Epstein’s victims.

articles.title_orig: Beijing drills water cannons and drones near disputed South China Sea shoals
articles.title_zh: Beijing drills water cannons and drones near disputed South China Sea shoals
articles.content_orig:
Training off Second Thomas and Sabina shoals tests small boats, surveillance drones and simulated vessel boardings amid ongoing spats
China’s coastguard has carried out an exercise featuring water cannons and drones near two disputed reefs at the centre of its simmering South China Sea contention with the Philippines to prepare for “foreign infringement”, according to state media.
A China Coast Guard flotilla “recently” conducted “comprehensive maritime law-enforcement training” in the waters around Second Thomas Shoal and Sabina Shoal, according to state broadcaster CCTV, which did not specify dates.
The official television network stated that the drill had focused on foreign vessels “illegally” entering the waters around the two shoals, while covering surveillance, tracking, maritime traffic control and tactical manoeuvres by small boats.
It also included practising water cannon use, drone operations and optoelectronic evidence collection – a technique that uses optical and electronic sensors to detect and record evidence that may not be visible to the naked eye – according to the report.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu’s bloc loses parliamentary majority, Justice Department subpoenas California officials
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu’s bloc loses parliamentary majority, Justice Department subpoenas California officials
articles.content_orig:
As coalition negotiations loom and allegations of foreign election interference emerge, Fox News Digital reporter Efrat Lachter reports from Tel Aviv, Israel.
Israel's final election count has confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has lost its parliamentary majority, but whether opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot can assemble a government to replace him remains an open question as negotiations begin behind closed doors.
The completed count, published early Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee , gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition alliance. The two predominantly Arab parties secured a historic 19 seats, placing them in a potentially decisive position.
Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest individual party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad with 12. Final voter turnout reached 77.9%, according to the Central Elections Committee results .
ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW
Posters of former Israeli Chief of General Staff and Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot, right, and Prime Minister and Likud Party leader Benjamin Netanyahu are seen as election campaigns intensify two days before the vote as campaign posters of candidates are displayed on billboards and buildings across the streets ahead of the Knesset elections scheduled for October 27, in Tel Aviv, Israel, on October 25, 2026. (Nir Keidar/Anadolu via Getty Images)
But the numbers leave neither major bloc with the 61 seats required for a majority, opening a complex political struggle involving potential partnerships with Arab parties, ultra-Orthodox lawmakers or a unity government bringing together longtime rivals.
A source familiar with opposition discussions, who spoke to Fox News Digital on condition of anonymity, described the outcome as a "bitter stalemate," but not an impossible political situation.
The source said opposition leaders are approaching coalition negotiations with patience and experience rather than treating the inconclusive results as a defeat, arguing that the next government could depend on their ability to forge partnerships that previously seemed unlikely.
FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER
An ultra-Orthodox Jewish man holds his ballot as he votes in the parliamentary election at a polling station in Jerusalem on January 22, 2013. Israelis voted on Tuesday in an election widely expected to win Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a third term in office, pushing the Jewish State further to the right, away from peace with Palestinians and towards a showdown with Iran. (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters)
In a potentially significant development Friday, Israeli journalist Yishai Cohen of Kikar HaShabbat reported that Rabbi Dov Lando, a leading ultra-Orthodox religious authority, had instructed lawmakers from Degel HaTorah, part of United Torah Judaism, to open discussions with the opposition.
According to the report, the objective is to reach an arrangement protecting the status of yeshiva students amid the longstanding dispute over mandatory military service.
Channel 12 reported that figures within the ultra-Orthodox party were considering allowing an Eisenkot-led minority government to survive through outside parliamentary support, potentially breaking with Netanyahu.
"Our votes are not in Netanyahu's pocket," party figures told Channel 12, according to a translation of the Hebrew-language report.
However, the office of United Torah Judaism Chairman Yaakov Asher denied that any instruction to begin negotiations had been issued.
Such an arrangement would represent a significant shift from the party's longstanding alliance with Netanyahu. Eisenkot's pledge to expand military conscription among ultra-Orthodox men remains a major obstacle, although Channel 12 reported that party figures were willing to consider a compromise on the issue.
The source familiar with opposition discussions told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot's camp had been preparing for the possibility of cooperation with ultra-Orthodox parties well before the election, suggesting that some of the options now being discussed had already been under consideration behind the scenes.
According to the source, such an arrangement could require compromises over military service and potentially outside parliamentary support from Arab lawmakers, bringing together political factions whose positions appeared irreconcilable during the campaign.
FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE
People gather near a pre-election campaign banner featuring leaders of the Joint List, ahead of Israel's national election, in Nazareth, Israel, on October 10, 2026. (Ammar Awad/Reuters)
Another possibility rests with the Arab parties, which nearly doubled their parliamentary representation from 10 to 19 seats following a surge in turnout.
But the prospects of an Arab-backed government have drawn conflicting assessments.
Channel 12 reported Thursday that Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas had expressed deep skepticism about the possibility of establishing an Eisenkot-led minority government supported by Arab lawmakers.
Israeli political commentator Amit Segal also argued that the available options had narrowed considerably, identifying a Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity government or another election as the two principal remaining possibilities.
Mohammed Majadla, head of the news division at Radio Nas and a Channel 12 political commentator, offered a different assessment in an interview with Fox News Digital, arguing that both Ra'am and the Joint List were prepared to use their parliamentary influence to prevent Netanyahu from returning to power.
"The two Arab lists agree on two things," Majadla said in the Hebrew-language interview. "First, they are prepared to do everything within the political process to ensure Netanyahu does not return to power."
According to Majadla, that could include joining a coalition, providing outside parliamentary support or abstaining from key votes.
He said their second shared priority was avoiding another election, which Arab political leaders fear could reverse their gains.
"The ball is now in Eisenkot's court, not in the Arab parties' court," Majadla said. "As far as the Arab parties are concerned, I can tell you they are truly prepared to do everything to make this happen."
Majadla suggested that public declarations should not necessarily be treated as final positions, particularly as parties seek leverage during coalition negotiations.
The difficulties extend beyond the Arab parties. Eisenkot's potential partners include politicians who strongly oppose cooperation with ultra-Orthodox factions, while several opposition leaders campaigned against relying on Arab lawmakers to govern.
NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING
A road sign stands in front of a large billboard featuring Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, right, of the Likud Party and former military chief and leader of the centrist Yashar Party, Gadi Eisenkot, in Ramat Gan on October 20, 2026. Israel heads to the polls on October 27 in its first election since the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack, in what is seen as a referendum on the prime minister. (Jack Guez / AFP via Getty Images)
A national unity government involving Likud and Yashar would offer a more straightforward mathematical route to a majority, but would require Eisenkot to reconsider his campaign pledge not to join a Netanyahu-led government.
For Netanyahu, the lengthy coalition formation process could provide additional opportunities. If Eisenkot receives the mandate to form a government but fails, President Isaac Herzog could assign the task to another candidate, potentially giving Netanyahu another chance to assemble a coalition. articles.title_orig: Binance Suspends Transactions After It Is Targeted in Biggest-Ever Cyber Heist
articles.title_zh: Binance Suspends Transactions After It Is Targeted in Biggest-Ever Cyber Heist
articles.content_orig:
The digital currency exchange Binance says it was the target of a $6.3 billion crypto heist Thursday, believed to be the largest ever recorded.
The company has suspended all deposits and withdrawals while it works with law enforcement to secure its infrastructure and locate stolen funds.
The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”
“The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X .
About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said.
Binance will “cover all losses” from the hack, it said, adding, “User funds are safe.”
“We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice,” it said.
Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange.
Unlike traditional bank deposits, funds kept in accounts with companies like Binance are not automatically insured against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges.
The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025.
Binance cautioned that the full value of assets affected by the hack, as well as assets recovered or frozen, could change.
“ This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” it said.
As word of the hack spread online Thursday, major cryptocurrencies traded lower. Bitcoin was down about 4.3%, while Ethereum lost 4.6% of its value.
Two major stablecoin issuers, Tether and Circle, said they had identified billions of dollars in assets connected to the hackers and had frozen them.
Tether froze more than $1.567 billion worth of its digital currency, CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X .
Jeremy Allaire, CEO of stablecoin issuer Circle, said the company had also frozen hundreds of millions of dollars of assets and was coordinating with law enforcement.
The massive breach of Binance occurs at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence.
Digital currency has been a primary target of hackers for years. In 2025, Coinbase disclosed that thieves had stolen customers’ personal information and tried to extort the company for $20 million . Coinbase refused to pay and offered a bounty for information leading to arrests, instead.
Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”
Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money-laundering laws. President Donald Trump later granted him a full pardon .
David Ingram is a tech reporter for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Chinese Executive Close to Nvidia CEO Suspected of Giving China Information
articles.title_zh: Chinese Executive Close to Nvidia CEO Suspected of Giving China Information
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang reported to have had close relationship with tech company executive suspected of passing intel to China
US intelligence agencies believe the Nvidia chief executive, Jensen Huang, has been targeted by an alleged Chinese spy who had done business with him, according to a new report by the New York Times.
Alice Huang or Huang Le, of no relation to the Nvidia CEO, is an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China , prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her. Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.
In the course of their surveillance, American officials determined that Alice Huang developed a close relationship with Nvidia’s CEO, according to the Times. Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom and have vaulted Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Donald Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.
White House officials are reportedly alarmed by Alice Huang’s access to the head of Nvidia precisely because of the close relationship he has developed with Trump, according to the New York Times.
The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions.
In a statement to the New York Times, Nvidia said there was nothing out of the ordinary about the Nvidia CEO’s interactions with Alice Huang.
after newsletter promotion
“Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” the spokesperson said in a statement. Megaspeed and customers like it “receive ordinary business information – not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets – and zero information relevant to national security”.
